formCues: Keep elbows pinned to sides
Use overhand grip on EZ bar
Curl without swinging torso
Squeeze forearms at top
setup: Stand holding an EZ curl bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, hands shoulder-width apart, arms extended.
commonMistakes: Using momentum to swing the bar
Letting elbows drift forward
Using too much weight and shortening range of motion

formCues: Keep upper arms vertical and stationary
Lower bar toward forehead under control
Extend elbows fully at top
Keep elbows tucked, not flared
setup: Lie on a flat bench holding an EZ bar with a shoulder-width grip, arms extended straight up over the chest.
commonMistakes: Flaring elbows out to the sides
Letting upper arms drift back over the face
Using shoulders to help press instead of triceps

formCues: Keep chest pinned to the pad
Curl bar up without moving upper arms
Squeeze biceps hard at the top
Lower under control to full extension
setup: Lean chest-first against an angled spider curl bench or incline bench, arms hanging straight down holding an EZ bar.
commonMistakes: Lifting chest off the pad to cheat the rep
Using momentum instead of a controlled curl
Not achieving full elbow extension at bottom

formCues: Pull bar up close to the body
Lead with elbows, keep them above wrists
Stop around chest height
Keep core braced and torso upright
setup: Stand holding an EZ bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip in front of the thighs.
commonMistakes: Pulling bar too high, straining shoulders
Using back swing for momentum
Letting elbows drop below wrists

formCues: Wrap wrist over the bar rather than fingers only
Keep shoulders engaged, not fully passive
Maintain a straight body line
Breathe steadily throughout the hold
setup: Grip a pull-up bar with the wrist rolled over the top so the palm faces down and the bar sits in the crook of the wrist, then hang with feet off the ground.
commonMistakes: Letting the grip slip into a normal hang
Fully relaxing shoulders into a dead hang
Holding breath during the hold

formCues: Stand tall with shoulders back
Grip dumbbells firmly at sides
Take controlled, even steps
Keep core braced throughout
setup: Stand between two dumbbells on the floor, hinge down to grip one in each hand, and stand up tall.
commonMistakes: Letting shoulders round forward
Taking uneven or rushed steps
Leaning to one side under load

formCues: Keep torso upright and braced
Grip handles firmly with neutral wrists
Walk with controlled, even strides
Keep shoulders packed down and back
setup: Stand between two loaded farmer's carry handles, squat down to grip them, and stand up to full height.
commonMistakes: Rounding the lower back on pickup
Walking too fast and losing control
Letting handles bang against the legs

formCues: Keep chest up and spine neutral
Grip kettlebell handles firmly
Take short, controlled steps
Keep core braced throughout the carry
setup: Stand between two kettlebells, hinge at the hips to grip the handles, and stand up tall.
commonMistakes: Letting kettlebells swing and bang into legs
Rounding the back during pickup
Shrugging shoulders up toward ears

formCues: Hinge and brace before lifting the bar
Stand tall with shoulders back once loaded
Take even, controlled steps
Keep grip firm and wrists neutral
setup: Stand inside a loaded trap bar, hinge at the hips to grip the handles, and drive through the legs to stand up.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back during the initial lift
Rushing the walk and losing posture
Letting the bar shift or tilt while walking

formCues: Keep body in a straight line from head to heels
Pull chest toward the bar
Squeeze shoulder blades together at top
Control the descent back to arms extended
setup: Lie under a fixed bar with feet elevated on a bench, grip the bar with an overhand grip, and hang with body straight.
commonMistakes: Letting hips sag toward the floor
Pulling with arms only, not engaging back
Shortening range of motion by not fully extending arms

formCues: Keep hips and shoulders square to the floor
Lift knee out to the side, not backward
Keep core braced to avoid rotating torso
Move slowly through the full range
setup: Start on hands and knees in a tabletop position with hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
commonMistakes: Rotating the hips to gain more height
Rushing the movement with momentum
Letting the supporting arm collapse

formCues: Wrap legs high around the upper arms
Press firmly through the hands
Lean weight forward as legs straighten
Keep core engaged to control the lift
setup: Sit with legs wide, place hands on the floor behind the legs, and hook the backs of the thighs over the upper arms.
commonMistakes: Placing hands too far from the body, losing leverage
Trying to straighten legs before engaging the core
Not warming up hips and hamstrings first

formCues: Arch upper back and lift chest
Rest crown of head lightly on floor
Keep legs active and together
Breathe fully into the open chest
setup: Lie on the back, place hands under the hips, and press onto the forearms to lift and arch the chest while tilting the head back.
commonMistakes: Putting excess weight on the head and neck
Forgetting to keep legs engaged
Rushing into the backbend without warming the spine

formCues: Pull chin above the bar before starting the hold
Keep elbows bent and chest up
Engage lats to resist descending
Keep shoulders pulled down away from ears
setup: Grip a pull-up bar overhand and pull up so the chin clears the bar, holding that top position.
commonMistakes: Letting chin drop below the bar too early
Shrugging shoulders instead of engaging lats
Swinging the body to extend the hold

formCues: Press lower back into the floor
Keep legs straight and low
Kick in small, quick alternating movements
Keep core braced throughout
setup: Lie on the back with legs extended and hands under the glutes or by the sides, lifting the legs slightly off the floor.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch off the floor
Kicking with legs too high, reducing core tension
Holding breath instead of breathing steadily

formCues: Position roller along the inner thigh
Support upper body with forearms
Roll slowly, pausing on tender spots
Keep hips relaxed and breathe steadily
setup: Lie face down with one leg bent out to the side and the foam roller positioned under the inner thigh.
commonMistakes: Rolling too fast to feel any release
Tensing the leg instead of relaxing into it
Applying too much pressure directly on the knee

formCues: Support body weight with hands behind hips
Place roller under the calf muscle
Roll slowly from ankle to knee
Rotate leg slightly to hit different angles
setup: Sit on the floor with the foam roller placed under one calf and hands planted behind the hips for support.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the back of the knee
Rushing through the movement
Not adjusting leg rotation to cover the whole muscle

formCues: Sit on the roller with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee
Lean slightly toward the tighter side
Roll slowly across the glute muscle
Breathe and relax into tender spots
setup: Sit on a foam roller, cross one ankle over the opposite knee, and lean back slightly onto the glute of the crossed leg.
commonMistakes: Rolling with too much speed
Staying too upright and missing the target area
Holding tension instead of relaxing into the pressure

formCues: Support weight with hands behind hips
Place roller under the back of the thigh
Roll slowly from knee to glute
Keep the other foot on the floor for control
setup: Sit on the floor with the foam roller under one hamstring and hands planted behind the hips.
commonMistakes: Rolling too quickly over tender areas
Letting the hips sag instead of staying supported
Rolling directly over the back of the knee joint

formCues: Support upper body on the forearm
Position roller along the outer thigh
Roll slowly from hip to knee
Keep core braced to control body weight
setup: Lie on one side with the foam roller under the outer thigh, propped up on the forearm with the top leg crossed in front for balance.
commonMistakes: Rolling too fast, causing sharp discomfort
Letting hips sag toward the floor
Spending too long directly on the knee

formCues: Lie on the side with roller under the armpit region
Extend the top arm overhead
Roll slowly along the side of the ribcage
Breathe steadily to help the muscle release
setup: Lie on one side with the foam roller placed under the lat muscle just below the armpit, extending the top arm overhead.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the ribs instead of the muscle
Moving too quickly to allow release
Holding breath during the roll

formCues: Keep chin tucked and core engaged
Roll only through the mid to lower back muscles
Avoid rolling directly on the spine
Move slowly and control the motion with the legs
setup: Sit on the floor with the foam roller behind the lower back, feet planted and knees bent, supporting the head with the hands.
commonMistakes: Rolling directly over the spine
Using too much speed and losing control
Overarching the lower back during the roll

formCues: Cross ankle over opposite knee for targeting
Sit directly on the roller at the glute
Roll slowly and pause on tight spots
Lean into the target side for more pressure
setup: Sit on a foam roller, cross one ankle over the opposite knee, and lean toward the crossed side to target the piriformis.
commonMistakes: Not crossing the leg, missing the deep muscle
Rolling too fast to allow release
Applying pressure directly on the sit bone

formCues: Stack shoulders directly over elbows
Press firmly through forearms into the floor
Engage core and squeeze legs together
Keep gaze fixed on a still point
setup: Kneel and place forearms on the floor shoulder-width apart, then kick up into an inverted balance on the forearms.
commonMistakes: Letting elbows splay wider than shoulders
Overarching the lower back once inverted
Kicking up with too much force and losing control

formCues: Brace core fully before lifting the frame
Keep torso upright and chest tall
Take short, deliberate steps
Grip handles firmly throughout the carry
setup: Stand inside a loaded carrying frame, squat down to grip the handles, and drive up through the legs to stand.
commonMistakes: Rounding the back during the lift-off
Rushing steps and losing balance
Letting the frame tilt or sway while walking

formCues: Ease into the stretch gradually, never force it
Keep hips square to the front
Engage the surrounding muscles slightly for control
Breathe deeply to help ease tension
setup: Lower into a front or middle split position, using hands on the floor for support and sliding only as deep as mobility allows.
commonMistakes: Forcing depth beyond current flexibility
Letting the hips rotate out of alignment
Bouncing instead of holding a steady stretch

formCues: Keep heels grounded if possible
Press elbows against inner knees
Lengthen spine and lift chest
Bring palms together at heart center
setup: Stand with feet slightly wider than hip-width, squat down fully, and bring palms together in front of the chest.
commonMistakes: Letting the heels lift excessively off the floor
Rounding the spine instead of lengthening it
Letting knees cave inward

formCues: Extend the straight leg directly out to the side
Reach the top arm overhead in line with the ear
Keep hips facing forward, not rotated
Lengthen through both sides of the torso evenly
setup: Kneel on one knee, extend the opposite leg straight out to the side with the foot flat, and reach the same-side arm overhead while leaning sideways.
commonMistakes: Rotating the hips instead of staying square
Collapsing into the side body instead of lengthening
Placing the extended foot at the wrong angle, straining the knee

formCues: Lower slowly from a hang into shoulder extension
Keep arms straight throughout
Relax shoulders gradually into the stretch
Keep core lightly engaged for control
setup: Start hanging from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip, then rotate the shoulders to lower the body into an inverted-arm hang behind the bar.
commonMistakes: Dropping into position too quickly without control
Forcing depth before shoulder mobility allows it
Letting the grip loosen during the hold

formCues: Turn toes out and bend knees over toes
Keep chest lifted and spine tall
Sink hips to about knee height
Press through the whole foot
setup: Stand with feet wide, toes turned out, and lower into a wide squat with hands at chest or reaching overhead.
commonMistakes: Letting knees cave inward past the toes
Leaning the torso forward instead of staying upright
Not sinking hips deep enough to load the legs

formCues: Lengthen the spine before rotating
Rotate from the torso, not by pulling with arms
Keep both sit bones grounded
Turn head last, following the rotation
setup: Sit with one leg extended, cross the opposite foot over the extended knee, and twist the torso toward the bent knee.
commonMistakes: Rounding the spine instead of sitting tall
Forcing the twist with the arms instead of the torso
Lifting the grounded sit bone off the floor

formCues: Interlace fingers and place crown of head on the floor
Stack hips over shoulders once inverted
Engage core and squeeze legs together
Keep weight distributed between head and forearms, not head alone
setup: Kneel and interlace fingers on the floor, placing the crown of the head between the hands, then walk feet in and kick up to invert.
commonMistakes: Placing too much weight directly on the head
Overarching or under-engaging the core once inverted
Kicking up with excess force and losing control

formCues: Keep spine tall and shoulders relaxed
Sit between the heels, not on them
Keep knees pointing straight ahead
Use a block under the hips if needed for comfort
setup: Kneel with knees together and feet slightly wider than hips, then sit back between the heels.
commonMistakes: Forcing the sit without enough ankle or knee mobility
Letting the spine round forward
Placing excess pressure directly on the knees

formCues: Start in downward-dog-like position with hips high
Sweep chest down and forward in an arcing motion
Rise into an upward-facing stretch at the bottom
Reverse the arc back to the starting position
setup: Begin in a pike position with hips lifted high and hands and feet on the floor.
commonMistakes: Rushing the arc and skipping the full range of motion
Letting the lower back sag excessively at the bottom
Not lifting hips high enough at the start

formCues: Bend knees and keep weight centered over the blades
Push off at an angle with each stride
Keep core engaged for balance
Swing arms in rhythm with the stride
setup: Stand on ice wearing skates, with knees slightly bent and weight balanced over the blades before pushing off.
commonMistakes: Standing too upright, reducing balance and power
Leaning too far forward and losing control
Tensing up instead of staying relaxed through the stride

formCues: Rotate the torso to drive each paddle stroke
Keep core braced for stability
Use the whole arm and back, not wrists alone
Maintain a tall, balanced posture
setup: Sit or stand on the watercraft with the paddle gripped shoulder-width apart, core braced and posture upright.
commonMistakes: Paddling with arms only instead of rotating the torso
Slouching and losing core stability
Gripping the paddle too tightly, causing fatigue

formCues: Keep eyes on the kettlebell throughout
Hinge the torso sideways while pressing
Keep the pressing arm locked as the body moves under it
Maintain a braced, stable base with the legs
setup: Clean a kettlebell to the rack position at the shoulder, then set feet and prepare to hinge sideways under the bell.
commonMistakes: Losing sight of the kettlebell during the movement
Bending the pressing arm instead of keeping it locked
Rushing the hinge without control

formCues: Keep elbows pinned to the sides
Curl with control, avoiding swing
Squeeze biceps at the top
Lower slowly to full extension
setup: Stand holding a kettlebell in each hand at the sides with a neutral or supinated grip, arms extended.
commonMistakes: Swinging the torso to generate momentum
Letting elbows drift forward during the curl
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom

formCues: Keep legs straight and off the bench
Brace core hard to prevent arching
Lower bar under control to the chest
Press bar back up in a straight line
setup: Lie on a flat bench with legs extended straight out, feet off the bench or floor, gripping the barbell above the chest.
commonMistakes: Letting the lower back arch excessively without leg drive to stabilize
Losing bar path control without leg support
Using too much weight before mastering the stability demand

formCues: Scoot hips close to the wall
Rest legs straight up against the wall
Relax arms out to the sides
Breathe slowly and let the body settle
setup: Sit sideways next to a wall, then swing legs up the wall while lying back onto the floor.
commonMistakes: Positioning hips too far from the wall, causing strain
Tensing the legs instead of relaxing them
Holding breath instead of breathing deeply
